summary.headline: PNB Q2 FY27: net profit INR 5,532 crore (+12.8% YoY), domestic NIM up 10 bps QoQ to 2.74%, GNPA down to 2.55%.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong Q2 FY27 with NII of INR 11,601 crore (+10.8% YoY, +7.4% QoQ) and operating profit of INR 7,532 crore, with core operating profit up 29.4% YoY. Domestic NIM rose to 2.74% from 2.64% QoQ, helped by FCNR(B) funds replacing high-cost bulk deposits and CDs, and by shedding low-yielding advances. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.55% and net NPA at 0.25%, while credit cost was about 0.25% after extra provisions. Treasury income was hit by G-Sec yield hardening, and analysts questioned the reconciliation of the INR 817 crore NPA provision against INR 97 crore P&L provision.

financial_highlights.change: Above INR 7,500 crore for 3 consecutive quarters

financial_highlights.metric: Core operating profit (ex recoveries and treasury)

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Advances INR 13.41 lakh crore, +14.7% YoY (+17.4% excluding a INR 23,700 crore IBPC reduction). Retail ex-IBPC +16.3%, MSME +19.8%, agriculture +18.1% YoY. Management targets RAM at 58-59% of the book by year-end.

segments.name: Deposits and CASA
segments.commentary: Global deposits INR 17.77 lakh crore, +9.9% YoY. Savings individual +8.4% QoQ growth; SA institutional down 3.84%; CASA growth 7.33%. CD ratio 75.5%; bulk plus CD share of deposits about 17%, down from about 19%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book INR 36,000 crore vs INR 18,300 crore a year earlier (about 97-98% YoY); 74% agri. Average yield about 8.6%, with management guiding to 8.75-8.9%.

segments.name: Fee and cards
segments.commentary: Fee income +16% YoY. Credit cards about 11 lakh (from 8 lakh in March 2026). Supply chain finance sanctions above INR 7,600 crore with INR 5,000 crore outstanding.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income INR 753 crore per CFO, versus INR 1,700 crore a year earlier. The MD cited INR 2,193 crore in the segment result, which the analyst disputed; the CFO said he would follow up. AFS reserve moved to negative INR 1,286 crore from positive INR 463 crore.

guidance_outlook: Domestic NIM expected to rise a further 7-9 bps in Q3 FY27 from the 25 bps repo hike, with about 56% of the book repo-linked; management said a minimum 7 bps NIM improvement is expected.
Global NIM guidance 2.6-2.7% for FY27 seen as achievable from 2.58% in Q2.
Credit cost guided at 0.25-0.30% after about 15 bps ECL-related impact; ROA above 1.04-1.05% and ROE of about 15-17% minimum expected.

ECL transition requirement revised to about INR 8,000 crore, with about INR 5,000 crore still needed after INR 2,560 crore floating provision and INR 1,150 crore standard-asset provision. Management said HTM impact is outside this and under RBI discussion.
Recovery target for FY27 revised to INR 12,000-13,000 crore (from over INR 14,000 crore); next year's target about INR 12,000 crore.
Branch opening target of 250 in FY27; 162 opened so far, 119 in South and West.
Credit growth 13-14% expected; no deposit rate hikes planned near term; target CASA-led deposit growth of 8-9%.
capex_capacity: Branch network: 162 of 250 targeted FY27 branches opened, 119 in Southern and Western regions.
Digital sanctions above INR 41,500 crore in H1 FY27, with a target of adding another INR 1 lakh crore in the year; 95% of customer transactions are digital.
PNB One business app has 4.14 lakh customers and 225+ features; UPI enabled for current account customers.
Quantum-safe encryption deployed in 246 customer-facing applications; Quantum Finance Innovation Hub at Amaravati.
Wealth management launch targeted from January; trade finance module revamp moving to mobile in about 2 months.
Corporate sanctions of over INR 2.5 lakh crore in H1 FY27 against INR 4 lakh crore in FY26; pipeline INR 1.58 lakh crore.
demand_pricing: Deposit cost falling: domestic cost of deposits 4.97% (Q2) vs 5.02% (Q1) and 5.18% a year earlier; domestic cost of funds 4.34% vs 4.57%.
FCNR(B) raised USD 2.7 billion against a USD 2.5 billion target, fully used to replace bulk deposits and CDs; about 30% self-funded, 70% leveraged.
Management is shedding low-yielding corporate advances (INR 58,000 crore cited) and replacing them with higher-yield sanctions.
Corporate growth would otherwise have been 17-18%; management said the book would reach 58-59% RAM by year-end, versus about 40-41% for many corporates.
Slippage in one corporate road/infrastructure account (about INR 300 crore, domestic); management attributed it to a one-off and said there is no Middle East impact.

qa_highlights.question: How was the FCNR(B) money used, and how much high-cost deposit is left?
qa_highlights.answer: USD 2.7 billion raised and fully used to shed bulk deposits and CDs; bulk plus CD share about 17% vs about 19% last quarter, CD down from about INR 60,000 crore to INR 40,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the NIM improvement and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances rebalancing and repricing of the repo-linked book, with a 25 bps repo hike and about 56% of the book repo-linked. Management expects a 7-9 bps NIM gain next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the reported provision only INR 97 crore when NPA provisions were INR 817 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: A INR 798 crore write-back from one investment-related account, a standard account per one answer, netted against the INR 817 crore loan provision; the CFO said investment provisions were netted in Schedule 8. A separate reconciliation was requested.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and how much provision is left to make?
qa_highlights.answer: ECL requirement about INR 8,000 crore, now about INR 5,000 crore after the INR 2,560 crore and INR 1,150 crore provisions; INR 100-150 crore more to be added over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SMA position?
qa_highlights.answer: Total SMA-0/1/2 at 2.49% (INR 33,410 crore): SMA-0 1.26%, SMA-1 0.56%, SMA-2 0.67%. Stress in agriculture in Maharashtra and Andhra is being monitored, with no restructuring started.

qa_highlights.question: How do the gold loan and fee businesses contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan INR 36,000 crore, average yield 8.6%; credit cards about 11 lakh; supply chain sanctions INR 7,600 crore with INR 5,000 crore outstanding; cards expected to add about INR 200 crore fee income next year.

risks_watch: Treasury income depressed by G-Sec yield hardening (negative MTM); AFS reserve moved to negative INR 1,286 crore; a further 30-40 bps yield hardening was flagged.
Agriculture stress in drought-affected districts; SLBC restructuring framework not yet in place.
Recovery shortfall versus target (INR 5,600 crore in H1 vs INR 13,000 crore target) and falling recoveries that could raise credit costs.
HTM-related ECL impact still under discussion with RBI; ECL outcome to be seen.
Unreconciled P&L vs balance-sheet provision (INR 817 crore vs INR 97 crore) and treasury income figures (INR 753 crore vs INR 2,193 crore) that analysts queried; CFO to follow up.
Falling SA institutional deposits and rising deposit cost pressure on NIM if deposit growth is pushed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, asset quality and credit growth, but evasive on several numbers (provision and treasury reconciliation, a ROE target that was restated) and deferred some follow-ups to the CFO.
key_quotes: Domestic NIM improved by 10 basis points sequentially from 2.64% to 2.74%, while global NIM increased from 2.5% to 2.58%.
Operating profit is continuously above INR 7,500 crores mark from the last 3 quarters and stands at INR 7,532 crores for Q2 of this year.
No, no, write-back of INR 2,000 crores is not there in NPA.

We have utilized this quarter. We have utilized in this quarter, and you must have seen in the note also we have mentioned that INR 1,150 crores, we have made a provision in the standard provision now.
Ashok Chandra: Going forward also, we are not going to increase the deposit rate.
Otherwise, the treasury profit would have been more than INR 1,700 crores, because last year in the same quarter, INR 1,700 crores was our treasury income.

adds.what: Branch network: 250 branches targeted in FY27, 162 opened so far (119 in South and West)

growth.why: Management guides credit growth of 13-14% (midpoint 13.5%) and a further 7-9 bps domestic NIM expansion in Q3 FY27 from the repo hike, backed by 162 of 250 FY27 branch openings, a 97% YoY gold loan book rise and FCNR(B) funding replacing bulk deposits, though no specific order or capacity numbers were given for the credit growth.
